done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The parser still mishandles Done-when inputs. `FISCAL_PERIOD_PATTERN` recognizes `FY` and `financial year` but not “fiscal year”, so “Show fiscal year 2025” reaches `YEAR_PREFIX_PATTERN` via `year` and replaces the model window with calendar 2025. That prefix also accepts `of` without checking what follows the number, so “Show an amount of 2025 rupees” is incorrectly interpreted as calendar year 2025, violating the requirement that an amount is never a year. Additionally, “Q3, 2025” detects Q3 but rejects the comma-separated year and anchors the quarter to the prior/current year. These deterministically return the wrong periods on the provider path.
findings.title: Not done: Named periods must override the model while fiscal and amount wording retain the model window

findings.body: The new coverage still calls `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`; unchanged lines 947-1033 show that the LLM, executor, audit, dimensions, and selection resolver are fakes. The frontend period-control tests also mock `api.ask` (`frontend/src/features/assistant/ask-panel.test.tsx:33`), while the repository has no Playwright configuration/specification or browser-test script and the root suite runs Node/Vitest tests only (`package.json:26`). Consequently, named-period follow-ups, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and changing the period control remain unproven through the required browser, running API, real database, and prior-turn transport. The successful hermetic close run does not satisfy that required user-flow proof.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
